Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bayesmaDatR 0.1.0

  • Initial release: workbook-to-model data manager for Bayesian meta-analysis.
  • launch_data_entry() is the card-based workbook manager from bayesma’s data entry app, rebuilt on the bayesmaDatR schema: upload a workbook or map columns from any XLSX/CSV/RDA/RDS file, edit Study Details, Outcome Details, Risk of Bias (all robbR tools, with coloured rating buttons and guides) and INSPECT-SR, sync studies across sections, validate, preview and download bayesma data, and download the workbook, single sections or a template.
  • Study Details gains n_periods; the mean cluster size is N / (n_clusters x n_periods), with 1 period for cluster trials and 2 for cluster crossover trials when it is missing.
  • merge_ma_data() (and the single-sheet workbook) now has one row per study, with each outcome’s columns side by side, suffixed by outcome (e.g. n_int_hosp_los).
  • write_ma_workbook(object_name = ) and the app name the data frame(s) in an .rda file; prefixed section names (e.g. los_studies) are recognised on upload.
  • Missing variances (e.g. no SD or IQR) no longer stop an export: the study is kept, yi/sei are left empty where they cannot be calculated, and a warning names the missing fields. MedD failures also warn.
  • Exports and Study Details downloads use a fixed column order: study_id, author, year, trial_design, control, intervention, n_int, n_ctrl, n_clusters, rho_w, rho_b, rho_wp (empty design columns omitted), extra study columns; then each outcome’s outcome_id, measure, n_int … q3_ctrl, design_effect, yi, sei; then risk-of-bias columns.
  • Import: “Other columns to keep” brings in any study columns (e.g. subgroup1, subgroup2) under their own names. subgroup and follow_up are no longer template fields.
  • launch_data_entry() opens in the web browser by default, as RStudio’s viewer cannot save downloads; failed downloads show the error in the app.
  • The app’s export “Format” offers a package-neutral “Standard” layout and MetaStan.
  • as_bayesma() exports several outcomes side by side in wide format: one row per study, outcome columns suffixed with the outcome (yi_hosp_los, sei_icu_los, …). Study rows with no reported data for an outcome are left out of it with a message. The app’s export takes several outcomes.
  • design_effect is always calculated (read-only in the app, not imported).
  • Import: each outcome block has its own sheet, header row and study identifiers; the column tag re-matches when changed and matches tags in the middle of names (e.g. Mean_LOS_ICU_int).
  • Study Details holds study-level n_int, n_ctrl, n_clusters, rho_w, rho_b and rho_wp; outcome rows inherit them where their own cells are empty (fill_study_defaults()), so outcome-specific values only need entering where they differ. cluster_size is replaced by n_clusters; the mean cluster size is derived as N / clusters (N / (2 x clusters) for cluster crossover trials). The Outcome Data download includes the inherited values.
  • write_ma_workbook() and the app’s workbook download can save an .rda file (one data frame per section, or one merged data frame).
  • Missing design-effect inputs give a design effect of 1; cluster crossover trials without rho_b use rho_b = 0. Outcomes carry a design_effect column, filled on import, by fill_design_effect() or the app’s “Recalculate design effect” button; a typed value is used as given.
  • Trial design codes are normalised (e.g. CXRCT, XRCT, cluster crossover become cxo_rct, xo_rct); CLARITY’s yes/no answers map to its judgements (e.g. “Probably no” is Probably high).
  • Imports drop columns that were skipped (left empty); “Manage columns” has a “Drop empty columns” button. Tables have row checkboxes for removing several rows at once.
  • trial_design now lives in Study Details (an outcome-level value still overrides it). Outcomes gain cluster_size for the design effect.
  • compute_design_effect() ports bayesma’s design effects; compute_effect_size(), as_bayesma() and as_MetaStan() use effective sample sizes for yi/sei (design_effect = "ignore" to switch off) and keep the reported n_int and n_ctrl alongside n_int_eff, n_ctrl_eff and design_effect.
  • as_MetaStan() exports one outcome in MetaStan’s arm-based format (arm 1 = control, multi-arm supported) and, by default, runs MetaStan::create_MetaStan_dat().
  • merge_ma_data() combines every section into one data frame; write_ma_workbook(layout = "single") writes it as one sheet.
  • App: hide skipped fields while mapping, fill a new Study Details column from the uploaded file, choose bayesma or MetaStan and the design effect when exporting, and download the workbook as separate sheets or one sheet.
  • split_iqr() and split_range() split Q1/Q3 or min/max reported in one cell; the importer does this for iqr_* and range_* columns.
  • Import mappings can take several columns per field, using the first non-empty value per study (e.g. an outcome-specific N, then the overall N). The outcome column tag (e.g. hosplos) matches columns such as N_hosplos_int ahead of N_int.
  • Continuous outcomes carry mean/SD, median, quartiles and range together; as_bayesma(estimate_means = "wan"/"qe") and the app’s export card estimate missing means and SDs for MD/SMD. convert_median_to_mean() fills both arms by default.
  • Imports can take each section from its own file and sheet, with a header row per section so title rows above the column names are skipped. Recognised sheets (studies, outcomes, risk_of_bias, inspect_sr) can be loaded as-is without replacing the other sections.
  • Workbook schema with outcome-specific sample sizes, mean/SD, median/quartile/ range, event and person-time summaries, trial_design (rct, xo_rct, c_rct, cxo_rct), rho_w/rho_b/rho_wp, and int_arm/ctrl_arm for multi-arm studies.
  • read_ma_workbook(), write_ma_workbook(), map_ma_columns(), sync_ma_data() and validate_ma_data().
  • Risk of bias for the eight robbR tools: rob_tools(), rob_domains(), rob_judgements() and add_rob() with rob_level = "study" or "outcome".
  • compute_effect_size() (OR, RR, IRR, MD, SMD, MedD) using bayesma’s rules and convert_median_to_mean() (Wan or QE via metamedian).
  • select_outcome(), prepare_arm_data(), prepare_outcome() and the as_bayesma() exporter (wide or long, one- or two-stage).
  • INSPECT-SR sheet with the 21 assessment items and auxiliary calculation fields.

Developed by Benjamin Moran.
